samples.summary: Autofit commit now writes x/y from an enter-time frame snapshot, so it can revert a position change made during the edit session
samples.evidence: `localFrame` is captured once at enter-text-editing time from a `store.read()` snapshot (`packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:4223` → `:4293`), and the commit callback runs arbitrarily later (`:4400`). Previously the commit patched only `{ h }`, so `MemSlidesStore.updateElementFrame` / `YorkieSlidesStore.updateElementFrame` merged the new h onto whatever LIVE x/y the element then had (`packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:708`, `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:1456`). It now also writes `x: fit.x, y: fit.y` computed from the stale snapshot, so any x/y change that landed between entering the edit and committing — a remote collaborator move over Yorkie, or a format-panel position commit (`packages/frontend/src/app/slides/format-panel/index.tsx:144`) while the element is selected and being edited — is silently overwritten back to the enter-time position (plus the rotation compensation). Fix belongs on the new code: re-read the element's current local frame inside the batch instead of closing over `localFrame`.

samples.summary: Live autofit-grow underlay still grows h with x/y held fixed, so it no longer matches the committed anchored frame on a rotated text box
samples.evidence: `maskEditingElement` renders the in-edit text box's decoration with `{ ...el.frame, h: Math.max(MIN_TEXT_BOX_H, liveHeight) }` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:7436), driven every keystroke from `render()` at :1541. That is exactly the size-only growth the delta removed from the commit path: it grows about the unrotated top-left in local terms, i.e. it moves the painted centre of a rotated box. Since the commit now anchors the unrotated top-left instead (`:4431`), the live preview and the committed render for a rotated text box differ by the compensation vector, so the box fill/border visibly jumps at commit — the same #1039 symptom, just moved to the preview→commit transition. Fix belongs on the preview: build the live frame with `resizeFrameToSize(el.frame, el.frame.w, liveHeight)`.

samples.summary: Panel rotate-90 still reads frame.rotation unguarded, so the legacy missing-rotation case this delta hardens against persists NaN rotation from the same panel
samples.evidence: The delta's premise (resize.ts:87-100, frame-patch.ts doc block, docs/design/slides/slides-format-options-panel.md:256) is that a legacy/imported frame can lack `rotation` and that persisting a NaN geometry field makes the element vanish. `rotate90` in the same format panel computes `((el.frame.rotation + delta) % (Math.PI * 2) + Math.PI * 2) % (Math.PI * 2)` and writes it straight through `store.updateElementFrame(..., { rotation: next })` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/format-panel/index.tsx:162-165). Note packages/frontend has no tsc lane, so nothing else flags this.

samples.evidence: docs/design/slides/slides-format-options-panel.md:252-254 asserts "crop commit and multi-resize already write whole frames, so they were never affected", and :259 lists the functions normalized to `?? 0`. But `frameRotationBasis` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:7320-7328) computes `cos: Math.cos(frame.rotation)` / `sin: Math.sin(frame.rotation)` with no `?? 0`, and its result flows into `windowToFrame` and then a persisted `{x,y,w,h}` patch at :2600-2605. verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described: `store.read()` returns a deep clone (memory.ts:147-157), so `localFrame` captured at editor.ts:4293 is an enter-time snapshot; the later `onCommit` batch (editor.ts:4400-4437) writes `x: fit.x, y: fit.y` derived from that stale snapshot. Both store implementations merge the partial patch onto the live frame (memory.ts:708, yorkie-slides-store.ts:1456), so previously patching only `{h}` preserved live x/y while the new code overwrites it. Concurrent x/y writers exist outside the diff and are reachable while the element is selected/edited: format-panel `translate` (format-panel/index.tsx:144, editing element is force-selected at editor.ts:4311) and remote Yorkie peers via yorkie-slides-store.ts:1430. No guard prevents an x/y change between edit entry and commit, and the clobber applies even at rotation 0. Impact (silently reverting a committed or remote position) is major under the blast-radius rubric as a violated cross-module invariant, so it stays in the gate.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described. maskEditingElement builds the live in-edit frame as `{ ...el.frame, h: Math.max(MIN_TEXT_BOX_H, liveHeight) }` (editor.ts:7434-7437) — size-only growth with x/y pinned, no rotation compensation. Meanwhile the commit path now anchors the unrotated top-left through resizeFrameToSize (editor.ts:4431), which per resize.ts:127-131 delegates to frameAtAnchor(start,'se',w,h) and is identity on x/y only at rotation 0 (documented resize.ts:118-125). The divergence is visible because the renderer really rotates about the centre (view/canvas/element-renderer.ts:205,216). No guard elsewhere reconciles preview with commit, so the underlay is a genuine untouched site left out of step with the changed contract — in-lane for blast radius and major impact.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. index.tsx:162-165 computes `((el.frame.rotation + delta) % (Math.PI*2) + Math.PI*2) % (Math.PI*2)` and writes it via `store.updateElementFrame(..., { rotation: next })` with no `?? 0` and no finite check, so an absent `rotation` persists NaN. The path is reachable from the UI: size-position-section.tsx:177 and :188 bind the rotate buttons to `onRotate90`, wired to this callback at index.tsx:285. No guard makes it unreachable: MemSlidesStore.updateElementFrame (memory.ts:691-743) merges the patch verbatim (`e.frame = { ...e.frame, ...frame }`) with only a connector-type rejection and no numeric validation, and consumers (element-renderer.ts:216, frame.ts:31,80) then compute NaN geometry. The premise is the repo's own: frame-patch.ts:19-25 and resize.ts:71-75/94-100 both explicitly harden against a legacy/imported frame lacking `rotation`, and the diff's new guard at frame-patch.ts:33 protects only the size-patch path (used by commitFrame index.tsx:128 and lockedResize index.tsx:237) while the sibling rotate control in the same panel bypasses any equivalent normalisation. This is squarely the blast-radius lane ("a new guard with a way around it") and major impact (persisted NaN rotation = vanished element). Only residual doubt is how commonly a stored frame omits `rotation`, which is a frequency question, not a refutation.

finding.summary: Text autofit-grow commit still writes a size-only frame patch, bypassing the new anchored-size contract for rotated text elements
finding.evidence: The diff establishes a repo-wide contract in `packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/resize.ts:117-118`: "Callers that write `w`/`h` on a rotated frame must go through this (or `resizeFrameWorld`) rather than patching size alone." An existing caller does exactly that: `packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:4420` commits `store.updateElementFrame(slideId, elementId, { h: targetH })` on text-edit exit. That path is only gated on `!ancestorHasTransform` (ancestor group transform, editor.ts:4417) — the element's OWN `frame.rotation` is not considered — so a rotated top-level textbox that autogrows keeps `x`/`y` fixed while its height changes, which moves the centre and shifts the painted box in world space: the exact defect #1039 fixed for the panel. The live ghost at `editor.ts:7420` (`{ ...el.frame, h: Math.max(MIN_TEXT_BOX_H, liveHeight) }`) has the same uncompensated shape. Fix belongs at the editor call site (route through the newly exported `resizeFrameToSize`), not in the diff's new code. Pre-existing behaviour, but it is the one remaining caller left outside the contract this change introduces.

verdict.reason: The claimed bypassing site does not exist as described. editor.ts:4417-4437 does NOT commit `{ h: targetH }` alone: it computes `const fit = resizeFrameToSize(localFrame, localFrame.w, targetH)` and writes `{ x: fit.x, y: fit.y, h: targetH }` — i.e. the text autofit-grow commit already goes through the anchored-size contract declared at interactions/resize.ts:115-131 (resizeFrameToSize -> frameAtAnchor; imported at editor.ts:107). The exact fix the finding prescribes ("route through the newly exported resizeFrameToSize") is already present at the cited call site, so the headline claim of a size-only frame patch is not present in the repo. The secondary site (editor.ts:7434-7437 in maskEditingElement, reached via editor.ts:1537-1541) does keep x/y while overriding h, but it is a transient in-memory render mask for the underlay decoration during editing — no store write, no persisted geometry — so under the blast-radius rubric it is at most a "still works but out of step" minor paint inconsistency, not the major broken caller asserted, and it is not the location the finding says must change.
